title: Most Probable Number (MPN) Method for Estimating Colony Forming Units of Piscirickettsia salmonis
author: Pamela Aravena

steps.title: Grow P. salmonis culture
steps.instruction: Grow a culture of P. salmonis in NPB medium (30 gr/L Tryptic Soy Broth, 256.6 mM NaCl, 8.25 mM L-cysteine, 37 µM FeCl3).

substeps.instruction: Inoculate a 50 mL tube containing 5 mL NPB with bacteria from a solid NPA plate (NPB + 1.5% agar) or from a grown NPB culture (OD~1.2-1.5).
Incubate at 18 °C and 180 rpm for 4 days.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial aliquots
steps.instruction: Take an aliquot (approximately 100 µL) of each culture to be tested for serial dilutions.

substeps.instruction: Store the aliquot at 4 ºC or on ice until use.

steps.title: Infect SHK-1 cell cultures
steps.instruction: Infect SHK-1 cell cultures at 80% confluence in a T75 flask using stationary state bacterial cultures at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100.

steps.title: Treat infected cultures with gentamicin
steps.instruction: Three days post-infection, wash the cultures with PBS and incubate for 40 minutes with Leibovitz's L15 medium containing gentamicin (100 µg/mL) at 18 ºC.

steps.title: Recover cells in fresh medium
steps.instruction: Wash the cells with PBS and incubate at 18 ºC with 15 mL of fresh Leibovitz's L15 medium supplemented with 5% FBS (without antibiotics).

substeps.instruction: Incubate for the required duration (e.g., 7 days after infection/dpi) at 18 ºC.

steps.title: Lyse cell monolayer
steps.instruction: Incubate the infected cell cultures with 1X cold PBS and lyse the monolayer by adding 4 mL of 1.5% Triton X-100 into the flask.

steps.title: Recover and concentrate bacteria
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire supernatant to a 50 mL sterile centrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Wash the flask twice with PBS and add the washings to the same 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the samples for 3 min at 1,000 x g.
Recover the supernatant and centrifuge again at 8,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in NPB.
Place on ice or at 4 ºC until use.

steps.title: Prepare 96-well plate for MPN
steps.instruction: Fill a 96-well round-bottom plate with 180 µL of NPB or the desired culture medium for testing P. salmonis replication.

steps.title: Perform serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Inoculate the first well (A1) with 20 µL of the grown P. salmonis culture or the recovered P. salmonis cells from infected SHK-1 cultures.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize the inoculated well by pipetting.
Serially dilute the culture 1/10 in each subsequent well until the 11th well (A11) to obtain dilutions 10^-1 to 10^-11.
Repeat the process for two or four more replicates (rows B-C or B-E) to obtain triplicates or quintuplicates.
Leave the 12th column of each row without inoculum as a negative control.

steps.title: Incubate and record growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 18 ºC without agitation for 7-10 days.

substeps.instruction: Record the number of wells with visible growth for every dilution in each replicate.

steps.title: Calculate MPN using R
steps.instruction: Calculate the Most Probable Number (MPN) using the MPN R package v0.3.0 or the EPA online calculator.

substeps.instruction: Install R Studio Desktop 1.1.463 and run: install.packages(c("MPN", "data.table")).
Prepare an input table with columns for dilution levels, number of replicates, and one column per sample indicating the number of positive results.
Save the table as 'MPN' in txt format and change the extension to TSV (tab-separated values).
Execute the provided R code using library(data.table) and library(MPN) with conf_level = 0.95 and CI_method = "Jarvis" to process 'MPN.tsv' and output 'MPN_out.tsv'.
